card: Adds a "never" option to the timestamp parameter in importdescriptors, allowing callers to completely skip blockchain rescanning during descriptor import. Currently, specifying "now" still forces a scan of the last two hours of blocks plus the mempool, adding latency when importing newly generated descriptors or when the user intends to rescan manually later. Links to issue #31263.
changed_since_previous: Expanded functional test coverage to include comprehensive cases for never, now, mixed batches, and subsequent manual rescanning.
evidence: PR description links to issue #31263 which requests an option to skip rescan during descriptor import.
problem: Callers importing descriptors known never to have been used, or wishing to defer rescanning until later, had no way to completely bypass the rescan in `importdescriptors`. Specifying "now" still rescans the blockchain from the last two hours (median time past) through the mempool.

risk.why: A flaw in the rescan trigger logic could incorrectly suppress rescans for other descriptors in a batch, leaving wallets oblivious to existing transactions.

summary: Adds support for "never" as an accepted value for the `timestamp` parameter in `importdescriptors`. Descriptors imported with `timestamp: "never"` do not trigger a blockchain rescan, allowing callers to bypass rescanning entirely if no other descriptor in the import request requires one.
